# Model and source

* Citation: `r rxode2::rxode2(readModelDb("Lanke_2019_tolvaptan"))$reference`
* Description: `r rxode2::rxode2(readModelDb("Lanke_2019_tolvaptan"))$description`
* Article: <https://doi.org/10.1002/jcph.1370> (open access, PMC6590359)

Lanke 2019 developed a population PK model of oral tolvaptan, the
vasopressin V2-receptor antagonist approved to slow kidney function decline
in autosomal dominant polycystic kidney disease (ADPKD), and validated it
externally against a separate phase 3b trial. The structural model is one
compartment with zero-order absorption (duration D1) directly into the
central compartment and first-order elimination. The distinguishing feature
is a relative bioavailability that falls with the amount administered,

$$F1 = \frac{Dose_{max}}{Dose_{50} + Dose}$$

(Lanke 2019 Equation 4), which the authors attribute to the low solubility
of tolvaptan. eGFR, body weight and CYP3A inhibitor coadministration act on
CL/F, and body weight acts on Vd/F.

# Population

The model was developed from 7335 plasma concentrations in 1091 adults with
ADPKD pooled from five phase 2 trials and the phase 3b open-label extension
NCT01214421 (Lanke 2019 Methods). Median age was 42 years (range 18-62),
median weight 79.5 kg (42.3-164.5), median BMI 25.9 kg/m^2 and median
CKD-EPI eGFR 69.4 mL/min/1.73 m^2 (13.62-137.37) (Table 1); 565 of the 1091
subjects were female and 18 were enrolled in Japan (Table 2). Of the 1073
subjects enrolled outside Japan, 1024 were White, 14 Black, 9 Asian,
1 Hispanic and 25 other. Doses ranged from single 15-120 mg doses to
split-dose regimens of 15/15 to 90/30 mg, the morning dose at about 8 AM and
the second dose 8-9 h later. 131 subjects had at least one record of CYP3A
inhibitor coadministration (3.46 percent of observations). External
validation used 678 subjects and 3012 observations from the randomized
withdrawal trial NCT02160145 at 60/30 or 90/30 mg.

The same information is available programmatically via
`readModelDb("Lanke_2019_tolvaptan")$population`.

# Source trace

| Element | Value | Source location |
|---|---|---|
| Structure: one compartment, zero-order input into central, first-order elimination | -- | Results, Base Model; Equation 5 |
| `lcl` (CL/F) | 12.6 L/h | Table 3, Final Model |
| `lvc` (Vd/F) | 110 L | Table 3, Final Model |
| `ld1` (D1) | 0.58 h | Table 3, Final Model |
| `lfdepot_dose50` (Dose50) | 166 mg | Table 3, Final Model; Abstract |
| `lfdepot_dosemax` (Dosemax) | 182 mg | Table 3, Final Model; Abstract |
| F1 = Dosemax / (Dose50 + Dose) | -- | Equation 4 |
| `e_crcl_cl` (eGFR power on CL/F) | 0.52 | Table 3; normalised to median 69.4 (Table 1, Equation 2) |
| `e_wt_cl` (WT power on CL/F) | -0.53 | Table 3; normalised to median 79.5 kg (Table 1, Equation 1) |
| `e_cyp3a4_inh_cl` (Inh on CL/F) | -0.23 | Table 3; linear form of Equation 3 |
| `e_wt_vc` (WT power on Vd/F) | 0.23 | Table 3; Equation 1 |
| `etalcl`, `etalvc`, `etald1` block | 0.40; -0.25, 0.49; 1.13, -1.51, 5.67 | Table 3, Interindividual variability |
| `etalfdepot_dose50` | 0.086 | Table 3 |
| `etalfdepot_dosemax` | 0.019 | Table 3 |
| `addSd` | sqrt(5.3) = 2.30 ng/mL | Table 3, Residual variability (variance) |
| `propSd` | sqrt(0.18) = 0.424 | Table 3, Residual variability (variance) |

The IIV entries are variances: `sqrt(0.49)` = 70 percent and `sqrt(5.67)` =
238 percent reproduce the Abstract's IIV for Vd/F and D1, and `sqrt(0.40)` =
63 percent is the Abstract's 64 percent for CL/F to rounding.

```{r model}
mod <- readModelDb("Lanke_2019_tolvaptan")
ui <- rxode2::rxode2(mod)
mod_typ <- rxode2::zeroRe(ui)
```

# Dose-dependent bioavailability

The Abstract states that F1 decreased by 36 percent as the dose rose from
15 mg to 120 mg, and the Results state that F1 equals 1 at the lowest dose
of 15 mg. Both follow from the Table 3 values. The function decreases
monotonically and has no minimum, so the Table 3 footnote's description of
Dosemax ("the highest dose at which F1 is lowest") does not describe it;
likewise F1 reaches 0.5 at 2 x 182 - 166 = 198 mg rather than at Dose50.

```{r f1}
f1 <- function(dose) 182 / (166 + dose)
f1_tab <- data.frame(dose_mg = c(15, 30, 45, 60, 90, 120)) |>
  dplyr::mutate(F1 = f1(dose_mg))
knitr::kable(f1_tab, digits = 3, caption = "Typical relative bioavailability by administered amount.")

stopifnot(
  abs(f1(15) - 1) < 0.01,
  # Abstract: 'F1 decreased by 36%' from 15 to 120 mg
  abs((1 - f1(120) / f1(15)) * 100 - 36) < 1
)
```

```{r f1-plot, fig.cap = "Typical relative bioavailability F1 versus the administered amount (Lanke 2019 Equation 4)."}
data.frame(dose = seq(0, 240, by = 1)) |>
  dplyr::mutate(F1 = f1(dose)) |>
  ggplot(aes(dose, F1)) +
  geom_line() +
  geom_point(data = f1_tab, aes(dose_mg, F1)) +
  labs(x = "Tolvaptan amount per administration (mg)", y = "Relative bioavailability F1") +
  theme_bw()
```

The same ratio must come out of the packaged model. Typical-value single
doses of 15, 30, 60 and 120 mg are simulated in a subject at the covariate
medians, and the PKNCA dose-normalised AUC is compared with the closed form
`F1(dose) x dose / CL`.

```{r single-dose}
sd_doses <- c(15, 30, 60, 120)
sd_times <- c(seq(0, 2, by = 0.02), seq(2.1, 24, by = 0.1), seq(24.5, 200, by = 0.5))
sd_events <- dplyr::bind_rows(
  data.frame(id = seq_along(sd_doses), time = 0, evid = 1, amt = sd_doses, rate = -2, cmt = "central"),
  tidyr::expand_grid(id = seq_along(sd_doses), time = sd_times) |>
    dplyr::mutate(evid = 0, amt = 0, rate = 0, cmt = "central")
) |>
  dplyr::arrange(id, time, dplyr::desc(evid)) |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    dose_group = paste(sd_doses[id], "mg"),
    DOSE_TOLVAPTAN_MG = sd_doses[id],
    WT = 79.5, CRCL = 69.4, CONMED_CYP3A4_INH = 0
  )

sd_sim <- as.data.frame(rxode2::rxSolve(mod_typ, sd_events, returnType = "data.frame",
                                        keep = "dose_group"))

sd_conc <- PKNCA::PKNCAconc(
  dplyr::filter(sd_sim, !is.na(Cc)) |> dplyr::select(id, time, Cc, dose_group),
  Cc ~ time | dose_group + id, concu = "ng/mL", timeu = "h"
)
sd_dose <- PKNCA::PKNCAdose(
  dplyr::filter(sd_events, evid == 1) |> dplyr::select(id, time, amt, dose_group),
  amt ~ time | dose_group + id, doseu = "mg"
)
sd_res <- PKNCA::pk.nca(PKNCA::PKNCAdata(
  sd_conc, sd_dose,
  intervals = data.frame(start = 0, end = Inf, cmax = TRUE, tmax = TRUE,
                         aucinf.obs = TRUE, half.life = TRUE)
))
sd_auc <- as.data.frame(sd_res) |>
  dplyr::filter(PPTESTCD == "aucinf.obs") |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    dose = sd_doses[id],
    closed_form = 1000 * f1(dose) * dose / 12.6,
    pct_diff = 100 * (PPORRES - closed_form) / closed_form,
    auc_per_mg = PPORRES / dose
  )
knitr::kable(
  sd_auc |>
    dplyr::select(dose_group, PPORRES, closed_form, pct_diff, auc_per_mg) |>
    dplyr::rename(
      "Dose" = dose_group, "AUC0-inf simulated (ng*h/mL)" = PPORRES,
      "AUC0-inf closed form (ng*h/mL)" = closed_form,
      "Difference (percent)" = pct_diff, "AUC per mg" = auc_per_mg
    ),
  digits = 2, caption = "Typical-value single-dose AUC0-inf from PKNCA against F1 x Dose / CL."
)

# Same parameters on both sides, so only quadrature error separates them.
stopifnot(all(abs(sd_auc$pct_diff) < 1))
auc_ratio <- with(sd_auc, auc_per_mg[dose == 120] / auc_per_mg[dose == 15])
stopifnot(abs((1 - auc_ratio) * 100 - 36) < 1.5)
```

The dose-normalised AUC at 120 mg is `r round(100 * auc_ratio, 1)` percent
of that at 15 mg, the 36 percent decrease the Abstract reports.

# Covariate effects (replicates Figure 1)

The Results give the covariate effects at the 5th and 95th percentiles of
eGFR (32 and 110 mL/min/1.73 m^2) and body weight (56 and 113 kg) relative
to the median subject; the Discussion gives the effect of inhibitor
coadministration. These are the bars of Lanke 2019 Figure 1.

The typical CL/F and Vd/F are read from a typical-value solve of the
packaged model for each covariate scenario, so the check exercises the
`model()` equations rather than a re-typed formula.

```{r covariates}
scen <- tibble::tribble(
  ~scenario, ~WT, ~CRCL, ~CONMED_CYP3A4_INH,
  "median", 79.5, 69.4, 0,
  "eGFR 32", 79.5, 32, 0,
  "eGFR 110", 79.5, 110, 0,
  "WT 56 kg", 56, 69.4, 0,
  "WT 113 kg", 113, 69.4, 0,
  "CYP3A inhibitor", 79.5, 69.4, 1
) |>
  dplyr::mutate(id = dplyr::row_number())
scen_events <- dplyr::bind_rows(
  dplyr::mutate(scen, time = 0, evid = 1, amt = 15, rate = -2),
  dplyr::mutate(scen, time = 1, evid = 0, amt = 0, rate = 0)
) |>
  dplyr::mutate(cmt = "central", DOSE_TOLVAPTAN_MG = 15) |>
  dplyr::select(id, time, evid, amt, rate, cmt, DOSE_TOLVAPTAN_MG, WT, CRCL, CONMED_CYP3A4_INH, scenario) |>
  dplyr::arrange(id, time)
scen_par <- as.data.frame(rxode2::rxSolve(mod_typ, scen_events, returnType = "data.frame",
                                          keep = "scenario")) |>
  dplyr::distinct(scenario, cl, vc)
ref <- dplyr::filter(scen_par, scenario == "median")
stopifnot(abs(ref$cl - 12.6) < 1e-6, abs(ref$vc - 110) < 1e-6)

cov_tab <- tibble::tribble(
  ~parameter, ~covariate, ~published_pct,
  "CL/F", "eGFR 32", -33,
  "CL/F", "eGFR 110", 27,
  "CL/F", "WT 56 kg", 20,
  "CL/F", "WT 113 kg", -17,
  "CL/F", "CYP3A inhibitor", -23,
  "Vd/F", "WT 56 kg", -8,
  "Vd/F", "WT 113 kg", 8
) |>
  dplyr::left_join(scen_par, by = c("covariate" = "scenario")) |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    value = ifelse(parameter == "CL/F", cl / ref$cl, vc / ref$vc),
    model_pct = 100 * (value - 1)
  )

knitr::kable(
  cov_tab |>
    dplyr::select(parameter, covariate, model_pct, published_pct) |>
    dplyr::rename(
      "Parameter" = parameter, "Covariate value" = covariate,
      "Model change (percent)" = model_pct, "Published change (percent)" = published_pct
    ),
  digits = 1,
  caption = "Covariate effects against the Lanke 2019 Results and Discussion."
)
stopifnot(all(abs(cov_tab$model_pct - cov_tab$published_pct) < 1))
```

```{r forest, fig.cap = "Replicates Figure 1 of Lanke 2019: change in CL/F and Vd/F at the 5th and 95th covariate percentiles. Dashed lines mark 80 and 125 percent."}
cov_tab |>
  dplyr::mutate(label = paste(parameter, covariate)) |>
  ggplot(aes(x = model_pct, y = reorder(label, model_pct))) +
  geom_col(width = 0.6, orientation = "y") +
  geom_vline(xintercept = c(-20, 25), linetype = "dashed") +
  labs(x = "Change from the median subject (percent)", y = NULL) +
  theme_bw()
```

The Discussion also gives CL/F of 14.7 L/h at 56 kg and 10.2 L/h at 113 kg
against "the typical value of 12.3 L/h". The model gives
`r round(scen_par$cl[scen_par$scenario == "WT 56 kg"], 1)` and
`r round(scen_par$cl[scen_par$scenario == "WT 113 kg"], 1)` L/h from the Table 3 value of
12.6 L/h; the ratios to the typical value agree to within 1 percent, and
only the typical value differs (see
Assumptions and deviations).

# Virtual cohort

97 percent of the development observations, and 93.7 percent of the
validation observations, came from the 60/30 and 90/30 mg split-dose
regimens, so the stochastic simulation uses those two arms with 200 subjects
each. Body weight is log-normal around the median of 79.5 kg with the
dispersion implied by the published 5th and 95th percentiles (56 and 113 kg);
eGFR is normal around 69.4 with the dispersion implied by its percentiles
(32 and 110), truncated to the observed range. CYP3A inhibitor
coadministration is drawn per subject with the 3.46 percent observation-level
frequency of Table 2 and held constant within a subject.

```{r cohort}
rxode2::rxSetSeed(20190501)
n_per_arm <- 200
regimens <- tibble::tribble(
  ~regimen, ~am_mg, ~pm_mg,
  "60/30 mg", 60, 30,
  "90/30 mg", 90, 30
)
cohort <- tidyr::expand_grid(regimen = regimens$regimen, subj = seq_len(n_per_arm)) |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    id = dplyr::row_number(),
    WT = pmin(pmax(79.5 * exp(rnorm(dplyr::n(), 0, log(113 / 56) / (2 * 1.645))), 42.3), 164.5),
    CRCL = pmin(pmax(rnorm(dplyr::n(), 69.4, (110 - 32) / (2 * 1.645)), 13.62), 137.37),
    CONMED_CYP3A4_INH = rbinom(dplyr::n(), 1, 0.0346)
  ) |>
  dplyr::left_join(regimens, by = "regimen")

knitr::kable(
  cohort |>
    dplyr::group_by(regimen) |>
    dplyr::summarise(
      n = dplyr::n(), WT_median = median(WT), CRCL_median = median(CRCL),
      CRCL_p05 = quantile(CRCL, 0.05), CRCL_p95 = quantile(CRCL, 0.95),
      inh_pct = 100 * mean(CONMED_CYP3A4_INH)
    ),
  digits = 1, caption = "Virtual cohort summary."
)
```

# Simulation

Fourteen days of split dosing: the morning dose at 0 h of each day and the
afternoon dose 8 h later, both as modelled-duration zero-order input
(`rate = -2`). `DOSE_TOLVAPTAN_MG` carries the amount of each administration,
so the morning and afternoon doses get different bioavailabilities. Day 14
(312-336 h) is sampled densely.

```{r simulate}
n_days <- 14
ss_start <- (n_days - 1) * 24
ss_end <- n_days * 24
dose_rows <- cohort |>
  tidyr::expand_grid(day = seq_len(n_days) - 1, slot = c("am", "pm")) |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    time = 24 * day + ifelse(slot == "am", 0, 8),
    amt = ifelse(slot == "am", am_mg, pm_mg),
    evid = 1, rate = -2, cmt = "central"
  )
obs_rows <- cohort |>
  tidyr::expand_grid(time = c(seq(ss_start, ss_start + 2, by = 0.05),
                              seq(ss_start + 2.1, ss_start + 10, by = 0.05),
                              seq(ss_start + 10.1, ss_end, by = 0.1))) |>
  dplyr::mutate(evid = 0, amt = 0, rate = 0, cmt = "central")
events <- dplyr::bind_rows(dose_rows, obs_rows) |>
  dplyr::arrange(id, time, dplyr::desc(evid)) |>
  dplyr::group_by(id) |>
  dplyr::mutate(DOSE_TOLVAPTAN_MG = ifelse(evid == 1, amt, NA_real_)) |>
  tidyr::fill(DOSE_TOLVAPTAN_MG, .direction = "down") |>
  dplyr::ungroup() |>
  dplyr::select(id, time, evid, amt, rate, cmt, DOSE_TOLVAPTAN_MG, WT, CRCL,
                CONMED_CYP3A4_INH, regimen, am_mg, pm_mg)

sim <- as.data.frame(rxode2::rxSolve(
  ui, events, returnType = "data.frame",
  keep = c("regimen", "am_mg", "pm_mg")
))
```

```{r vpc, fig.cap = "Simulated day-14 tolvaptan concentrations by regimen: median and 5th-95th percentile band of the individual predictions (compare the external-validation VPC of Lanke 2019 Figure 2)."}
sim |>
  dplyr::filter(time >= ss_start) |>
  dplyr::mutate(tad_day = time - ss_start) |>
  dplyr::group_by(regimen, tad_day) |>
  dplyr::summarise(
    p05 = quantile(Cc, 0.05), p50 = median(Cc), p95 = quantile(Cc, 0.95),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  ggplot(aes(tad_day, p50)) +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = p05, ymax = p95), alpha = 0.25) +
  geom_line() +
  facet_wrap(~regimen) +
  scale_y_log10() +
  labs(x = "Time after the day-14 morning dose (h)", y = "Tolvaptan (ng/mL)") +
  theme_bw()
```

# PKNCA validation

Lanke 2019 reports no NCA summary for its simulations, so the steady-state
NCA is checked against the closed form it must satisfy instead. For any
subject at steady state the AUC over one day equals the bioavailable daily
amount divided by clearance,
`AUC0-24 = 1000 x (F1(AM) x AM + F1(PM) x PM) / CL`, whatever the
absorption duration. Both sides use the same drawn parameters, so the check
fails on a mis-applied bioavailability (for example the daily total instead
of the per-administration amount, or a bioavailability that is not evaluated
on its own dose record).

```{r pknca}
nca_conc <- sim |>
  dplyr::filter(!is.na(Cc), time >= ss_start) |>
  dplyr::select(id, time, Cc, regimen)
nca_dose <- events |>
  dplyr::filter(evid == 1, time >= ss_start) |>
  dplyr::select(id, time, amt, regimen)

conc_obj <- PKNCA::PKNCAconc(nca_conc, Cc ~ time | regimen + id, concu = "ng/mL", timeu = "h")
dose_obj <- PKNCA::PKNCAdose(nca_dose, amt ~ time | regimen + id, doseu = "mg")
intervals <- data.frame(start = ss_start, end = ss_end, cmax = TRUE, tmax = TRUE,
                        cmin = TRUE, auclast = TRUE)
nca_res <- suppressMessages(PKNCA::pk.nca(PKNCA::PKNCAdata(conc_obj, dose_obj, intervals = intervals)))
knitr::kable(summary(nca_res), caption = "Simulated day-14 NCA per regimen (one dosing day, 24 h).")
```

```{r closed-form}
indiv <- sim |>
  dplyr::filter(time == ss_start) |>
  dplyr::distinct(id, regimen, am_mg, pm_mg, cl, fdepot_dose50, fdepot_dosemax, d1)
chk <- as.data.frame(nca_res) |>
  dplyr::filter(PPTESTCD == "auclast") |>
  dplyr::select(id, regimen, auc_sim = PPORRES) |>
  dplyr::left_join(indiv, by = c("id", "regimen")) |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    auc_closed = 1000 * (am_mg * fdepot_dosemax / (fdepot_dose50 + am_mg) +
                           pm_mg * fdepot_dosemax / (fdepot_dose50 + pm_mg)) / cl,
    pct_diff = 100 * (auc_sim - auc_closed) / auc_closed
  )
knitr::kable(
  chk |>
    dplyr::group_by(regimen) |>
    dplyr::summarise(
      median_auc_sim = median(auc_sim), median_auc_closed = median(auc_closed),
      median_pct_diff = median(pct_diff), p90_abs_pct_diff = quantile(abs(pct_diff), 0.9)
    ) |>
    dplyr::rename(
      "Regimen" = regimen, "Median AUC0-24 simulated (ng*h/mL)" = median_auc_sim,
      "Median AUC0-24 closed form (ng*h/mL)" = median_auc_closed,
      "Median difference (percent)" = median_pct_diff,
      "90th percentile absolute difference (percent)" = p90_abs_pct_diff
    ),
  digits = 2, caption = "Steady-state AUC0-24 from PKNCA against the per-subject closed form."
)

# Centre and robust envelope only: subjects with a very long D1 (IIV variance
# 5.67) are still approaching steady state on day 14.
stopifnot(
  abs(median(chk$pct_diff)) < 1,
  quantile(abs(chk$pct_diff), 0.9) < 5
)
```

A typical subject at the covariate medians is checked the same way with no
random effects.

```{r typical-ss}
typ_events <- events |>
  dplyr::filter(id %in% c(1, n_per_arm + 1)) |>
  dplyr::mutate(WT = 79.5, CRCL = 69.4, CONMED_CYP3A4_INH = 0)
typ_sim <- as.data.frame(rxode2::rxSolve(mod_typ, typ_events, returnType = "data.frame",
                                         keep = c("regimen", "am_mg", "pm_mg")))
typ_chk <- typ_sim |>
  dplyr::filter(time >= ss_start) |>
  dplyr::group_by(regimen, am_mg, pm_mg) |>
  dplyr::summarise(
    auc_sim = sum(diff(time) * (head(Cc, -1) + tail(Cc, -1)) / 2),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    auc_closed = 1000 * (am_mg * f1(am_mg) + pm_mg * f1(pm_mg)) / 12.6,
    pct_diff = 100 * (auc_sim - auc_closed) / auc_closed
  )
knitr::kable(typ_chk, digits = 2, caption = "Typical-subject steady-state AUC0-24.")
stopifnot(all(abs(typ_chk$pct_diff) < 0.5))
```

## Comparison against published NCA

Lanke 2019 reports no Cmax, AUC or half-life values for tolvaptan, so there
is no published NCA table to compare against. The quantitative checks above
replace it: the 36 percent fall in F1 from the Abstract, the covariate
effects from the Results and Discussion, and the closed-form steady-state
exposure.

# Assumptions and deviations

* **Dose50 = 166 mg, not 160 mg.** The Results prose gives Dose50 as 160 mg;
  Table 3 and the Abstract give 166 mg. 166 mg is used because it makes F1
  equal to 1 at 15 mg (182 / 181 = 1.006), as the Results state, and
  reproduces the Abstract's 36 percent decrease from 15 to 120 mg (36.7
  percent); 160 mg gives 1.04 and 37.5 percent.
* **Residual error read as variances.** Table 3 prints Additive 5.3 and
  Proportional 0.18 without saying whether they are variances or standard
  deviations, and no control stream is published. They are read as NONMEM
  SIGMA variances (`addSd = sqrt(5.3)` = 2.30 ng/mL, `propSd = sqrt(0.18)` =
  0.424), consistent with the IIV block of the same table, which is provably
  on the variance scale. This was a maintainer ruling; it affects only the
  spread of simulated observations, not `Cc`.
* **Per-administration dose in F1.** Equation 4 does not say whether `Dose`
  is the amount of each administration or the daily total. The model uses the
  amount of each administration, carried in `DOSE_TOLVAPTAN_MG`, because the
  paper anchors F1 to the lowest single dose of 15 mg, which is also the
  smallest administration in any split regimen.
* **New parameter names.** `lfdepot_dose50` and `lfdepot_dosemax` were
  registered for the two dose-scale constants (maintainers' ruling), following
  the `lcl_dose50` grammar of the dose-dependent clearance family. The
  paper's own glosses for them ("the dose at which F1 is 50%", "the highest
  dose at which F1 is lowest") do not describe Equation 4.
* **Typical CL/F in the Discussion.** The Discussion computes the
  body-weight examples (14.7 and 10.2 L/h) from a typical CL/F of 12.3 L/h,
  whereas Table 3 gives 12.6 L/h. The model uses Table 3; the ratios are the
  same.
* **F1 is relative.** Only oral data were modelled, so F1 is relative to a
  15 mg administration and CL/F and Vd/F are apparent values.
* **Food not modelled.** Food intake was not recorded in the phase 3b trials,
  and the paper notes that a high-fat meal raised Cmax by 15-96 percent;
  there is no food effect in the model.
* **Virtual cohort.** Body weight and eGFR distributions are reconstructed
  from the published medians and 5th/95th percentiles; CYP3A inhibitor use is
  a per-subject indicator drawn at the observation-level frequency, whereas
  in the source data it changed record by record. The CYP3A4 inducer
  indicator, age, BMI, sex and Japan site were screened but are not in the
  final model.
